title: Wildfire risk and grid hardening costs
bottleneck: Utility-ignited wildfires have caused catastrophic losses, forcing utilities into expensive hardening: undergrounding lines at more than 3 million dollars per mile, covered conductors, and public-safety shutoffs that anger customers. California utilities alone plan tens of billions in wildfire spending, recovered through rates. Hardening reduces but does not eliminate ignition risk. Public-safety power shutoffs during fire weather impose their own economic costs, from spoiled food to idle businesses, concentrated on vulnerable communities.
why_it_blocks: Wildfire liability is reshaping utility finance. Hardening costs flow to ratepayers, raising electricity prices and eroding the affordability case for electrification.
current_state: Undergrounding and covered-conductor programs are underway. Ignition risk persists and cost-recovery battles continue. Insurers are repricing wildfire-exposed utility risk, adding financial pressure beyond the engineering costs.
